pr_body:
Fixes: https://github.com/swaywm/sway/issues/7936

In the transition to wlr_scene, I accidentally dropped a call to reset this `has_exclusive_layer` so once it was set, nothing could reset it afterwards and the compositor basically unusable. Let's just drop the has_exclusive_layer bool for something simpler and more robust.

Output of `WAYLAND_DEBUG=1 shotman --capture output`: https://paste.sr.ht/blob/22620559ee800e1996579f5d7206a4c5c7bad980

Note that I tested a merge of this into master: `Merge: dcdb7275 972fcc60`.

The (admittedly uncommon) scenario where two layer surfaces are competing for exclusive keyboard interactivity isn't handled so far in this implementation.

For instance, consider that a layer surface on layer `overlay` requests exclusive keyboard interactivity and while it still has it, a new layer surface on layer `top` also requests it. The [previous implementation](https://github.com/swaywm/sway/blob/2c69e19fd30c5ceac61d6af821c6c6875cd3f8b6/sway/desktop/layer_shell.c#L247-L279) considered layer ordering so the `overlay` layer surface was able to keep the exclusive keyboard interactivity, but on the PR as it stands the `top` layer surface can take it away.

Furthermore, in this scenario with two layer surfaces requesting exclusive keyboard interactivity, when the focused layer surface is closed, the previous implementation was able to give/return focus to the other layer surface, while the PR as it stands doesn't, and focus is given to regular (non-layer) surfaces.

If it's of any help, the way I am testing this is with [bemenu](https://github.com/Cloudef/bemenu), with two builds, a vanilla one and one with [the layer](https://github.com/Cloudef/bemenu/blob/f8b17fd861de1387e8d8d1c6989e3be0f1247bc4/lib/renderers/wayland/window.c#L442) changed to `top`.

review_comments:
Seems like we're loosing this condition here?

IOW, exclusive keyboard layers under the toplevels would never get focus before, but now they do.
Why do we have this condition in the first place?

That's a decision we made when implementing layer-shell support. The motivation is that if a particular layer has focus, a lower level layer cannot get focus. So if a toplevel has focus, background/bottom cannot get focus.
